title: Two Distinct Ledgers
mathematical_role: Place the arithmetic Mordell-Weil ledger and analytic L-function ledger side by side, with the BSD equality shown as a conjectural bridge rather than as a definitional identity.
learning_objective: Identify r_alg and r_an as independently constructed invariants and interpret BSD as the claim that they agree.
literal_semantics: Mordell-Weil gives E(Q) as a finitely generated abelian group with free rank r_alg.
Canonical heights feed the regulator on the arithmetic side.
The analytic side is assembled from prime point counts and Euler factors.
Modularity supplies analytic continuation and a functional equation.
r_an is the order of vanishing of L(E,s) at s=1.
nonliteral_semantics: The visual bridge does not prove or define the equality r_alg=r_an.
Panel size, shading, and placement do not rank the mathematical importance of the two constructions.
No numerical agreement is asserted for a specific curve.

notes: Candidate semantics are bounded by the existing documentary source; no new mathematical source is admitted by this visual operation.

accessibility.alt_text: Two labelled ledgers separate arithmetic rank and regulator data from analytic Euler-product and central-zero data, with a dashed BSD box asking whether r algebraic equals r analytic.
accessibility.long_description: The left panel records the finitely generated Mordell-Weil group, algebraic rank, canonical heights, regulator, and finite torsion subgroup. The right panel records prime point counts, Euler factors, modular continuation, the L-function, and analytic order of vanishing. A dashed center box labels r_alg ?= r_an as BSD, and a lower guardrail says the two ledgers must not be collapsed.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: The plate correctly distinguishes the two constructions whose rank invariants BSD conjectures to be equal.
not_claimed: That arithmetic rank is defined analytically
That analytic rank is defined arithmetically
The BSD equality for all curves

supersession_reason: Turn an atmospheric paired panorama into an explicit comparison of two independently defined ledgers and a clearly conjectural bridge.
